# Template recipes

## Choosing a starting point

Letters, reports, notes, theses, exams, and papers have different structures. Preserve the requested type rather than adding abstract, bibliography, or submission gates to every document. Select only a host-approved template ID supported by `latex_project init`; do not substitute an invented ID when a requested class is unavailable.

For official templates, record the verified source, applicable version/year, retrieval date, content hash, and relevant license. A bundled example or remembered venue rule is not current official evidence. Use only approved resource/provider channels; unavailable official evidence prevents a compliance claim, not unrelated draft writing.

## Migrating an existing document

Save the current snapshot and, if available, a matching baseline PDF. Read class options and project-local `.cls`/`.sty` usage, shared preamble, include structure, custom commands, theorem environments, bibliography style/backend, and engine/font choices. Identify compatibility work before replacing any template file.

Keep content migration separate from scientific rewriting. Preserve labels, citations, equations, author metadata required by the chosen stage, valid PDF/vector assets, and supplied `.bbl` files when needed for a source package. Approved class or style changes are protected and must pass the host gate. A source-level config edit does not by itself prove the host's registered target/toolchain changed; re-inspect and report any required host configuration.

## Verifying the migration

Use a clean build for each affected registered target. Check front matter, headings, equations, references, bibliography, appendices, tables, figures, and representative text pages. Page limits may exclude references or appendices; use the verified rule's scope rather than always total PDF pages.

Fix compatibility within the template contract. Never shrink official margins/fonts or delete substantive content to make a submission fit. Unverifiable venue rules, unavailable fonts, or unsupported engine configuration remain explicit review/provisioning items. Deliver draft evidence separately from any formal release assessment.
